description:
FILED s501 (Fable, 2026-09-30).  USER, on hearing the idea: "Neat, put it in the todo to try."  RUNTIME-ONLY; scheduled as the FILLER of perf round 38 (brief ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s501/s501q/prompt.md).

WHY: s494u (#2092 phase 1) made lc/uc/lcfirst/ucfirst/fc regime-aware.  The USER accepted its cost ("Keep them, :-(") -- bench, best of 5, two interleaved pairs, load 2-4, control band about +-2 %:
    ucshort  (many short PURE-ASCII uc/lc calls)      -4.4 / -10.3 % vs base 209e7533   (0.73x of perl: still faster than perl)
    lcbytes  (lc/uc/ucfirst over undecoded UTF-8)     -26.4 / -28.3 % vs base            (3.60x of perl; base's answers were WRONG there)
The cost is PASSES, not the rule.  Today (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, `%p-case-map` and its helpers):
    pure ASCII  = `%p-first-high-char` (one typed scan that finds nothing) + `string-upcase`/`string-downcase` (a second pass, through SBCL's Unicode-aware char mapping)
    UTF-8 bytes = `%p-first-high-char` + `%p-bytes-look-utf8-p` (validation) + `%p-case-map-ascii` (a REPLACE copy, then a mapping loop)  = four passes

THE IDEA (untried): ONE loop that maps and checks together.  Allocate the result; for each char: below #x80 -> store its ASCII case image by arithmetic (the `%p-case-map-ascii` test); at or above #x80 -> STOP the fast loop at index HI and decide the regime once, exactly as today (`%p-bytes-look-utf8-p s hi` under regime nil; never under :u):
    bytes   -> keep going in the SAME result: copy high chars unchanged, map ASCII ones (the prefix already written is right under both rules)
    Unicode -> the prefix is right too (ASCII maps the same under both rules); hand the TAIL (or the whole string, whichever measures faster) to string-upcase/downcase
A pure-ASCII string then pays ONE pass with arithmetic mapping and no scan -- possibly FASTER than base, whose string-upcase consults the Unicode tables per char.  The bytes path drops from four passes to two (map + validate the tail).  lcfirst/ucfirst look at one char: keep their `first-only` short cut, and check that the copy of the rest is one REPLACE.

MEASURE FIRST (the cheap discriminating measurement; take it before writing the real thing): a 20-line replica of the one-pass loop in a scratch .lisp, timed against `string-upcase` and against today's scan+`string-upcase` on (a) the four short words of the ucshort row, (b) an 80-char ASCII line, (c) the lcbytes line -- 5 M calls each, best of 5, a control pair.  If (a) is not at least as fast as plain `string-upcase`, STOP and write the numbers here: the scan was never the cost and the idea is dead.

SEMANTICS MUST NOT MOVE (perl -> base -> tree, byte-identical to the tree before the change): Pl/t/case-regime-01.t (37 rows) + utf8-source-01.t rows 42-46; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/d2092/rules.pl; Fable's review probes ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s500/review/r494u-regime.pl and r494u-break.pl (their outputs on the merged tree are the expected answers, INCLUDING the ruled divergences: error set (i) rows 7 10 12 of r494u-break, error set (ii) rows 3 17 21 25 of r494u-regime); non-simple strings (a fill-pointer buffer, a displaced capture -- 128dfd7b fixed the scan for those: keep a guard row); the empty string; a string whose ONLY high char is the last one; fc; `\L \U \l \u \F` (they share the function).  Rule 12: the regime dispatch keeps its dying arm.

BAR: runtime-only => `tools/corpus-diff.pl` IDENTICAL; check-parens; the gate; the full sweep (a cl/ change); companion op/lc.t uni/{fold,lower,upper,title}.t re/subst.t `--jobs 1` rows unchanged; bench A/B on a QUIET box (load < 2) with controls textproc subste strcat regexg: ucshort back inside the control band of the PRE-s494u base (209e7533) or better, lcbytes measurably better than the s494u tree, no control row slower.  Report the three numbers beside each other: 209e7533 / s494u tree / this.


=== DONE (s501q) -- in part: the BYTES arm only ===
REPLICA (the stop rule, scratch/s501q/case-replica.lisp): the one-pass short pure-ASCII loop 0.046 s vs string-upcase 0.048 s -- it passed.  IN THE RUNTIME it did not: bench `ucshort` read +21.1 % and +22.0 % in two interleaved pairs (load 1.4-2.1) against the base, so the short-string path (%p-case-map-short) was REMOVED again (78a911ce); string-upcase/downcase stays for pure ASCII.  The replica is not the runtime (the extra function boundary and the result allocation discipline cost more than the scan it saved).
SHIPPED: the undecoded-UTF-8 BYTES arm copies and maps in ONE loop (%p-ascii-case-char) instead of REPLACE + a mapping loop: `lcbytes` -13.3 % / -14.3 % (two pairs), -9.7 % in the runtime-only A/B after the removal.  Semantics: case probes (rules.pl, r494u-regime, r494u-break) byte-identical to the base; guard rows "#2535 case map" in perf-levers-07.t.  Three-number table (209e7533 / s494u tree / this): FINAL TREE (s503, 71bd29ef on main 2284d58d, quiet box load 0.8-1.7, bench-exec BENCH_K=5 two interleaved passes vs base-2284d58d, scratch/s501q/bench-final/table.txt): sigarith 0.1163 -> 0.0235 s (-79.8 %, 0.22x of perl), passarr 0.2683 -> 0.1683 (-37.3 %), listdeclcat 0.4491 -> 0.2213 (-50.7 %), lcbytes 0.1534 -> 0.1422 (-7.3 %; 209e7533 0.1134), ucshort 0.1074 -> 0.1077 (+0.3 %, ctl +1.2 %; 209e7533 0.1046), methret +2.0 % (rerun -2.1 %); real programs (realprog-final.txt, K=5): Air-mass 1.303 -> 0.979 s (-24.9 %), Perfect-shuffle 0.620 -> 0.437 (-29.6 %), Sub-unit-squares 0.425 -> 0.327 (-22.9 %), ctl <= 0.4 %; compile time +0.4 % wall over 111 files.  FLAGGED: fibret +4.3..5.4 % in bench-exec (direct timing +0.6..2.6 %; an identity parameter copy is not faster, so not #2570 -- cause not found)..
subject: PERF (try): lc/uc case mapping in ONE pass -- map ASCII by arithmetic while looking for the first high byte, instead of scan + string-upcase (pure ASCII) or scan + validate + copy + map (UTF-8 bytes); wins back s494u's ucshort -4..-10 % and lcbytes -26 %
